title: Add Quickstart Templates section + docs navigation updates
author: Elliot Price
release_notes: Docs: Introduces a Quickstart Templates section in navigation and links to the quickstarts repo + CLI install instructions.
body:
## Summary
This PR introduces a new **Quickstart Templates** section in the docs IA and updates navigation to make templates discoverable from the main sidebar and from relevant SDK pages.

Primary goal: reduce “where do I start?” friction by giving users a single place to find template options (RAG + agents first), and a clear path to either (a) use GitHub template repos directly or (b) use the template CLI.

## Motivation / context
DevEx is shipping production-minded quickstart templates (safe defaults, streaming robustness, observability hooks). The docs currently surface examples and SDK guides, but there is no dedicated landing area for templates, and no consistent navigation route from SDK pages.

This PR is the docs-side IA plumbing to support:
- A top-level landing page for templates
- A small set of child pages (initially stubbed/linked) that will be filled in by follow-up PRs
- A canonical link to the `redwood-quickstarts` repo and CLI installation instructions

Related:
- Docs IA proposal: sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/quickstarts-information-architecture-update.json
- Template project brief: sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/quickstart-templates-project-brief.json

## What changed
- Added **Quickstart Templates** to the left nav under “Quickstarts” (next to Examples)
- Added a landing page that:
  - Explains what templates are (opinionated scaffolds with production defaults)
  - Calls out initial template lineup focus: RAG + agents
  - Links to:
    - GitHub repo: `github.com/redwoodinference/redwood-quickstarts`
    - CLI install docs (new short page)
    - “Next steps” pointers: observability, safe defaults, deployment
- Added cross-links from SDK areas (where appropriate) pointing users to templates rather than duplicating setup instructions

## Notes on terminology
We use “templates” consistently and avoid implying “Agents” is a Redwood product feature. Copy uses “agent loop” / “tool-calling agent” wording.

## Changed areas / files (high level)
- docs navigation config
  - `content/config/navigation.yml`
  - `content/config/sidebar.quickstarts.yml`
- new pages
  - `content/quickstarts/templates/index.mdx` (landing)
  - `content/quickstarts/templates/cli-installation.mdx` (CLI install + basic usage)
- small cross-links
  - `content/sdks/python/index.mdx`
  - `content/sdks/typescript/index.mdx`

## Content outline (landing page)
- What you get (production defaults): timeouts/retries, streaming robustness, guardrails, OTel hooks
- What templates are not (not a managed product; you own the code)
- Choose your path:
  1) Use GitHub template repo
  2) Use `redwood-templates` CLI (`init`, with upgrade story noted as “coming soon”)
- Where to find help / issues: GitHub issues + docs troubleshooting page (to be added in follow-up)

## Checklist
- [x] Nav entry added and visible in dev build
- [x] Links resolve (repo + CLI page)
- [x] No duplicated setup steps; SDK pages now point to templates where relevant
- [x] Terminology consistent with DevEx guidance (RAG vs agent vs workflow)

## Preview
Local preview steps:
1) `pnpm install`
2) `pnpm dev`
3) Navigate: Quickstarts → Quickstart Templates

---

## Commits (summary)
1. docs(nav): add quickstart templates section to sidebar
2. docs(pages): add templates landing page
3. docs(pages): add CLI installation page + repo links
4. docs(sdk): add “Try the templates” cross-links from SDK index pages

---

## Review discussion

**Wei Chen (review):** The landing page copy is good, but please make sure we don’t oversell “production-ready” as a guarantee. Suggest adding a short disclaimer that teams should review defaults and threat model for their environment.

**Elliot Price (author):** Good call. Added a short “Review for your environment” callout under “What you get” and softened language from “production-ready” to “production-minded defaults”.

**Monica Patel (review):** Can we link to the CLI but keep it optional? Some users will be behind proxies and may prefer GH templates. Also please avoid implying `doctor/deploy/upgrade` exists.

**Elliot Price (author):** Updated the landing page to present GitHub templates as the first path, CLI as optional. CLI page only documents `init` and explicitly notes other commands are planned.

**Nikhil Sharma (review):** Please ensure Hosted API users have a clear next step without mentioning Dedicated/Private too prominently. We can add a brief “Deployment modes” mention, but keep it secondary.

**Elliot Price (author):** Adjusted ordering: Hosted API quickstart path first, then a short “If you’re on Dedicated/Private” section with a single sentence + link to existing deployment docs.

**Henry Cho (review):** Minor: add a link from templates landing page to the benchmarks/perf section later. Not required for this PR.

**Elliot Price (author):** Added a TODO note in the page frontmatter comments for follow-up PR; not adding a dead link right now.

---
